The served viewer is the OHIF bundle inside orthancteam/orthanc:24.12.0's libOrthancOHIF.so plus config/ohif.js; its decoder set must be read from the served bundle (the plugin's resources are compressed)

served CT frame throughput through E is lane-bound (R244-02): a frame holds the 4 B2 append lanes for 233 ms median (run e-route-diag2-opus-20261026a, 1200 frames: D current() twice 89, B2 per-transaction statements about 55, B2 append/result 29, B2 admissions twice 25, B2 identity 12, E preparation insert 24). E's part is cut by keeping one study-manifest copy (20261026210000); on the same 200 x 512x512 CT and the same #248 integration a first opening takes 20.7 s for all frames (mean of 7 openings, 19.7-22.1; before 22.2 s) and a repeated one 14.2 / 14.9 s (before 15.5 / 16.2 s), about 19 frames/s after the first image (before about 17), against 8.0 s / 7.8 s direct; the first image stays 8.5-11.3 s cold and 4.1-4.5 s repeated. The remaining cost belongs to D's current read (Orthanc QIDO and identity resolved twice inside the lane), the B2 transaction statements, admission and 4-lane bound (D1770), and the per-frame B2 events of E-02/E-03 (a recording-granularity decision); the first opening also waits for the whole-study catalog read

the pinned viewer's streaming frame loader (cornerstone dicom-image-loader streamRequest) stops reading at Content-Length without reading the end of the stream; Chromium then sometimes cancels a frame response it received whole (net::ERR_ABORTED, R244-03; 6 of 21 observed first openings, none of 10 repeated ones). The slice is in the viewer (run e-route-final6-opus-20261026a: the canceled slice's image is in the viewer's cache, 262144 pixels); the served test reads the viewer's state as well as the network events
